title: How a memory harness keeps long-running agents on track
subtitle: Sakana AI's on-device harness: core, recall and archival memory around small local research agents.
hook: A ranked ledger of past decisions beat vector RAG, letting a local model recall step 124 at step 500.

sources.title: Memory Harnesses for Long-Running Research Agents
sources.speaker: Stefania Druga

nodes.label: Research agent
nodes.detail: Small research agents with zero durable memory of their own, so every memory they use has to come from the harness.
nodes.tradeoff: On long tasks, context rot sets in: the model contradicts itself, redoes work, or drifts from the question.

nodes.label: Memory harness
nodes.detail: Memory is treated as a write, manage, read control loop around the model, not just a database. It logs each turn and assembles what the agent sees.
nodes.tradeoff: The model stays fixed across tasks; only the recall block's settings change between runs.

nodes.label: Core block
nodes.detail: A core block of traces that is always shown to the agent on every turn.
nodes.tradeoff: Core memory is always present; anything older must be fetched by the recall block.

nodes.label: Archival block
nodes.detail: Keeps track of information across different sessions, beyond a single run.
nodes.tradeoff: The open question is what survives when the agent runs over and over, across many sessions.

nodes.label: Recall policy
nodes.detail: Tested as a ladder: no recall, vector RAG, a ranked decisions ledger, and an oracle. Ranked-only recall performed best.
nodes.tradeoff: Ranking beat gating, where the harness first asks whether memory is needed at all.

nodes.label: Decisions ledger
nodes.detail: Records the decisions made on every turn so the harness can prioritise and rank them later.
nodes.tradeoff: Ranked recall was not just more accurate; it also cost less, because bad memory burns tokens.

nodes.label: Local model
nodes.detail: Runs on an M3 Ultra Mac with 96 GB: Qwen 27B quantised to 4-bit, and DeepSeek V4 Flash.
nodes.tradeoff: DeepSeek V4 Flash runs one query at a time with no batching, so evaluations take days.

nodes.label: Benchmark check
nodes.detail: A long-horizon memory benchmark: the answer sits at step 124, but the question comes at step 500. Run over 68 questions with many seeds.
nodes.tradeoff: The ranked-recall result held on both local models and on a second benchmark, Spider 2.

nodes.label: Oracle recall
nodes.detail: Hands the harness the correct memory for every loop, as a ground-truth reference for the other recall modes.
nodes.tradeoff: It still misses the max: the model can get the right memory and ignore it or get confused.

flow.text: At step 500, the agent is asked about something from step 124.
The harness has logged every turn's decisions as it went.
Step 124 sits in the ledger, far outside the context window.
The ranked policy pulls the best-matching past step back in.
Core traces are always shown alongside the recalled memory.
Qwen 27B, running locally, reads the packed context and answers.
The benchmark checks the answer against the true step.

takeaways.text: When the task fits in context, a memory harness adds cost but not capability.
Bad memory is expensive: it spends more tokens and can send the agent the wrong way.
Treat the recall policy as a first-class metric: what you store, how you rank, what you recall.
